prompt: CHALLENGE: You add 1.0 eq CH₃MgBr to methyl benzoate (PhCOOMe). What is the major isolated product after aqueous workup — the ketone (acetophenone) or the tertiary alcohol (2-phenyl-2-propanol)?

options.label: The tertiary alcohol (2-phenyl-2-propanol), with ~50% unreacted ester left over. The ketone intermediate (acetophenone) is MORE reactive than the ester, so once a bit of ketone forms, it consumes any available Grignard faster than the ester does.
The ketone, acetophenone, as the major product (clean 1-eq stop).

explanation: This is why Grignard + ester always 'adds twice' — the ketone intermediate is more electrophilic than the ester, so sub-stoichiometric Grignard still over-adds. To stop at a ketone, use a less reactive nucleophile like a Weinreb amide (RC(=O)N(OMe)Me) or Gilman reagent (R₂CuLi).
